scope: Checkpoint provenance, recorded offline training and deployment adapters. Metadata were inspected without model execution or training. Exact historical training-source and GLEET-history limits are distinguished from verified checkpoint and log identities.

trainingSet.scope: The recorded training minimized these 45 synthetic functions with box bounds, without UAV map objectives. The recorded logs store the indices of sampled functions and the last shuffled name list; they do not preserve every permutation. The retained trainers create fresh policies and do not load weights before training. Paper 3 uses the inherited final files directly, without training or checkpoint selection on its missions.

historicalSource.scope: The accepted Paper 1 catalog establishes exact weight identity. Companion HDF5 headers match the checkpoint timestamps. CPU times align closely with Paper 1 Table 6. The RLAM-PSO log is 18.11 CPU seconds below the value implied by 15.92 h in Table 6. The executed March source hash is not recorded. The retained April drivers match the frozen trainer files. The April benchmark loop calculates the AFSACPSO reward from the observation-boundary iteration; the later correction uses adjacent observations.

AFSACPSO.checkpointRule: Periodic saves overwrite the same filename. The trainer writes final weights after the last episode and saves the companion log. Held-out evaluation reads the fixed named files.
AFSACPSO.reward: Entropy-regularized SAC with relative best synthetic objective decrease 2*(Fbefore-Fafter)/(abs(Fbefore)+abs(Fafter)+1e-8). See historicalSource for the timing distinction.
AFSACPSO.normalization: Nine engineered swarm features clipped to [0,1]; eight-observation means and successive differences of the first three give six extra inputs, initially zero. No fitted input standardization.
AFSACPSO.adapter: Current UAV score, feasibility and penalty inputs feed the retained encoder. The deterministic tanh actor mean gives nine latent actions, expanded to per-particle coefficients using rank-normalized swarm geometry. Observations every 25 iterations, with legacy action timing and no learning.

SAC-SAPSO.checkpointRule: Periodic saves overwrite the same filename. The trainer writes final weights after the last episode and saves the companion log. Held-out evaluation reads the fixed named files.
SAC-SAPSO.reward: Entropy-regularized SAC with sign-aware relative incumbent improvement between observations (Eq. 25). Let B=abs(Fbefore)+abs(Fafter). Reward is zero if equal, 2*(Fbefore-Fafter)/(Fbefore+B+1e-30) for two positive values, 2*(Fbefore-Fafter)/(Fbefore+2*B+1e-30) for two negative values, and one otherwise, clipped to [-1,1].
SAC-SAPSO.normalization: Per particle, tanh(mean(abs(2*(v-(lower+upper)/2)/(upper-lower)))) across decision dimensions, with synthetic bounds for training and [1,mapSize] feature bounds repeated by waypoint for deployment. The other inputs are stable fraction, infeasible fraction and iteration progress. No fitted input standardization.
SAC-SAPSO.adapter: Current UAV route feasibility feeds the retained 103-state encoder. The deterministic tanh actor mean is affinely mapped to one coefficient triplet for the entire swarm. No rank residual or learning.

RLAM-PSO.checkpointRule: Periodic saves overwrite the same filename. The trainer writes final weights after the last episode and saves the companion log. Held-out evaluation reads the fixed named files.
RLAM-PSO.reward: DDPG reward +1 for an iteration with a global-best synthetic objective decrease >1e-6, and -1 otherwise.
RLAM-PSO.normalization: Iteration progress and stagnation normalized by iteration budget, and mean sample standard deviation of raw particle coordinates. Each scalar x is encoded as sin(2^k*x), k=0..4. Raw spread is not divided by map width.
RLAM-PSO.adapter: The common UAV score drives PSO. Twenty clipped actions control five interleaved groups with one coefficient triplet each. Gaussian exploration and learning are disabled.

GLEET.trainingEvidence: The README uses this file in a 10D CEC2021 F1 (Bent Cigar) DMSPSO rollout. The separate GPSO training example does not identify the run that produced the file. The paper describes T-step PPO and incumbent improvement normalized by initial best fitness. The file does not establish its training benchmark, backbone, reward settings, epoch or overlap with Paper 3 maps.
GLEET.checkpointRule: Use the supplied example checkpoint by fixed name and hash, strict actor loading and no gradient updates. No Paper 3 checkpoint selection or fine-tuning in the adapter.
GLEET.normalization: Concatenate nine current, nine personal-best and nine global-best features per particle. Fitness uses initial best score; budget and stagnation use run lengths; distances use the search-box diagonal; angles use cosine. Native layer mode standardizes per instance over particle and embedding dimensions.
GLEET.adapter: Native 15D GPSO, 100 particles, periodic boundaries, velocity clamp 10, inertia decay and one clipped Normal action per particle. Bridge affinely maps [-100,100]^15 to waypoint bounds and supplies the common UAV score.
